title: Security posture discovery with Vesta Healthcare
summary: Intro discovery focused on security posture for potential Redwood Hosted -> Dedicated migration. Main concerns: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC & audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and data retention policies for PHI-sensitive workloads. Action: send SOC 2 report, SAML integration guide, schedule technical deep dive and pilot scope.
next_steps: Jordan to send SOC 2 and ISO 27001 attestation docs
Priya to share SAML SSO quickstart + RBAC examples
Schedule SE deep dive and benchmark test with Ethan week of 2026-04-27
Customer to confirm PII/PHI retention window and compliance requirements
action_items: Jordan Meyers - Send SOC2 report and latest pen test summary (due 2026-04-22)
Priya Nair - Email SAML configuration docs and example metadata (due 2026-04-21)
Ethan Ross - Share current infra diagram and list of IP allowlists for pilot (due 2026-04-23)
Maya Patel - Confirm required retention period for logs and data (due 2026-04-24)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Liu Chen: Doing good, thanks. Appreciate the time.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Hi all, Maya here. We're primarily concerned with the security posture before we consider any hosted or dedicated deployment.
[00:22] Jordan Meyers: Totally, that's why we set this call. We wanted to run through SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit log retention, encryption/KMS — the usual security checklist. Priya will take the technical bits.
[00:35] Priya Nair: Hi team. Quick agenda: current stack, compliance evidence, auth/integration patterns, encryption and key mgmt, data residency & retention, and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:44] Ethan Ross: Yeah, go ahead. We're running a mix of on-premise Postgres and AWS EKS, some PHI flows, so we need to make sure any vendor can meet HIPAA-ish controls.
[00:55] Priya Nair: Understood. First — compliance attestations. Redwood has SOC 2 Type II; we also have an ISO 27001 cert for our control plane. I can share the reports after this call.
[01:06] Maya Patel: When you say share, are those redacted or full reports? We need the SOC 2 report plus the mapping to controls for HIPAA.
[01:15] Jordan Meyers: We usually provide the SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA and a controls mapping doc. For ISO we can share cert and scope. We'll include a whitepaper that maps Redwood controls to HIPAA requirements — note that we don't sign HIPAA BAAs on the hosted free tier, but enterprise contracts and Dedicated/Private options include BAA discussion.
[01:36] Maya Patel: Important. Our legal will want that. Also, audit logging retention — how long do you retain logs and can we customize?
[01:45] Priya Nair: Default audit logs retention is 90 days in the hosted plan; in Dedicated/Private you can extend retention and ship logs to your SIEM. For Dedicated we support pushing audit logs to customer's S3/CloudWatch/Elastic — or we can integrate with Splunk.
[02:00] Ethan Ross: For PHI we'll need longer retention for certain datasets and also immutable audit trails. Is immutability supported?
[02:07] Priya Nair: Yes, you can configure write-once object stores or route logs to your accounts where retention policies apply. For Hosted we offer tamper-evident logs with HMACs and a retained chain; for Dedicated you control the destination, so immutability is customer-managed.
[02:22] Liu Chen: KMS and encryption — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)? We don't want Redwood to hold keys for production PHI.
[02:30] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We support KMS integrations. For Hosted we offer BYOK where you provide a customer-managed KMS key in AWS KMS or a Cloud HSM; Redwood can use that for encrypting customer data at rest and for disk encryption on Dedicated. For Private deployments you fully control KMS.
[02:48] Maya Patel: Is there a limit to key rotation or support for automatic rotation?
[02:52] Priya Nair: Key rotation is handled by your KMS policy — Redwood supports rotation events and seamless re-encryption as long as key aliases are preserved. We'll document the steps in the guide.
[03:03] Jordan Meyers: Let's talk SSO. Do you use SAML? OIDC? We need to connect to Okta.
[03:10] Maya Patel: Okta and Azure AD are our sources. SAML is preferred for our internal console access.
[03:15] Priya Nair: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC for both console and API auth. For enterprises we recommend SAML with SCIM provisioning and RBAC. We'll share a SAML metadata XML and example attribute mapping.
[03:29] Ethan Ross: Do you support enforced MFA via the IdP and can you blacklist local login?
[03:35] Priya Nair: Yes, MFA is enforced at the IdP. We can disable local password auth for accounts and require SAML across the org. SCIM allows us to sync groups for RBAC rules.
[03:44] Maya Patel: Good. On RBAC — can we create fine-grained roles, e.g., read-only for analytics team, model deploy rights for a small set of users, and separate billing access?
[03:55] Priya Nair: We expose role templates and custom roles. Roles can be scoped to projects, models, and routes. Billing is a separate permission set. For Dedicated we can add custom RBAC integrations with your directory.
[04:08] Liu Chen: How are service-to-service tokens handled? We want short-lived tokens with rotation, not long-lived API keys.
[04:15] Priya Nair: We support short-lived tokens via a token exchange from your identity provider, plus session tokens issued by Redwood with TTLs you can set. For long-running jobs we recommend workload identities scoped to the job with limited privileges.
[04:28] Jordan Meyers: Any controls around inference data? For example, do you persist prompts/responses by default? For PHI we can't persist beyond certain retention windows.
[04:38] Priya Nair: By default Hosted retains transient logs for 30 days for debugging; you can opt out of retention or set to zero for sensitive routes. For Dedicated we give you full control over data retention and the option to disable persistent storage of input/output.
[04:53] Maya Patel: Is there a redaction or tokenization feature before logs are stored?
[04:58] Priya Nair: We have pre-storage hooks — you can run a transform that scrubs or tokenizes PHI before it hits storage. For our enterprise customers we can integrate with an on-prem tokenizer service via a secure connector.
[05:12] Ethan Ross: Network controls — need private connectivity, IP allowlist, and VPC peering options.
[05:18] Priya Nair: For Dedicated we support VPC peering and private endpoints. For Hosted we provide IP allowlist and private link in certain regions. Private deployment in your VPC/on-prem gives full network control.
[05:30] Liu Chen: Do you have penetration test results and vulnerability management cadence?
[05:34] Jordan Meyers: Yes, we run quarterly vuln scans and annual pen tests; we can share a summary and remediation timelines.
[05:41] Maya Patel: We will need a third-party pen test attestation as part of vendor onboarding.
[05:44] Priya Nair: We can provide the attestation under NDA. Also note our SLA and incident response playbook; we provide SOC 2 incident notifications and can offer an incident runbook tailored to you for Dedicated customers.
[05:59] Ethan Ross: Regarding model variants and fallbacks — any concern about data leaving the region? We need data residency assurances.
[06:06] Priya Nair: We support region pinning for inference and data storage. For Hosted we'll ensure data stays in the chosen region; Dedicated/Private gives you full control. If fallback to another region is configured we surface that and it's opt-in.
[06:18] Liu Chen: Audit logs — are they searchable and do you provide structured fields (user, ip, action, model, route, tokens)?
[06:25] Priya Nair: Yes — logs include structured fields: user_id, ip_address, action, model_id, route_id, request_id, and a hashed payload reference. We can forward logs to your SIEM with the full schema.
[06:37] Maya Patel: About SOC 2: do you have the SOC 2 for both control plane and data plane, or just control plane?
[06:44] Jordan Meyers: SOC 2 covers the control plane and managed hosted environment; we provide a data handling addendum and controls mapping. For Dedicated the controls shift — some controls are customer-managed, which we'll identify in the mapping.
[06:58] Ethan Ross: Can Redwood sign our standard DPA and security addendum?
[07:02] Jordan Meyers: We're generally able to sign standard DPAs and security addenda with enterprise contracts. For hosted self-serve there are standard terms; for Dedicated/Private we negotiate enterprise contracts that include those clauses.
[07:15] Maya Patel: One more — do you expose a history of admin actions? We need admin audit trails.
[07:21] Priya Nair: Yes, admin audit logs are available with details on who changed roles, who created API keys, and model rollout actions.
[07:31] Jordan Meyers: Ok, quick recap: we'll send the SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SAML quickstart and RBAC examples, and a doc on KMS/BYOK. We'll schedule a technical deep dive with Ethan to scope a pilot — likely Dedicated test pool or Private eval depending on the controls.
[07:51] Liu Chen: Sounds good. For the pilot, we want to test a small dedicated pool with region pinning, CMK, and SCIM-based RBAC.
[08:00] Priya Nair: Perfect; we'll prepare a pilot runbook and benchmark steps.
[08:05] Maya Patel: Please include expected timelines and who's responsible for each step. Also include any cost deltas for Dedicated security add-ons.
[08:13] Jordan Meyers: Will do. Any other questions?
[08:16] Ethan Ross: Not on my side.
[08:17] Maya Patel: No. Thanks.
[08:19] Jordan Meyers: Great, we'll follow up with artifacts and propose times for the SE deep dive. Thanks everyone.
[08:24] Liu Chen: Thanks all.
